summary: Two critics judge the round-6 lit Ember pair (pendant LIT and Core LIT-c: softboxes unseen, colour-only denoise, the Core key off) for the lamp pages' second pictures; a skeptic checks each
logs: lit pair r6 critics: 2 of 2 returned

findings.where: Core base body, the cone below the red band under the ball (full res x 520-1110, y 1530-1740)
findings.what: At 480 x 600 the base body reads as black or dark brown, not Ember. Body mean sRGB (22.2, 0.3, 0.2), L* 1.5, C* 7.1, the same at 480. None of its pixels reach R 40 at 480 (round 5: 98 %, body (47.7, 1.0, 0.8), L* 5.9, C* 24.9; OFF frame (153, 35, 33), L* 34). In the pair it is within 1.5 L* of the pendant's black cap, which is (0, 0.1, 0.2) at 480. Only the band under the ball shows that the base is red. This is not a realism fault: as a photograph it holds together (see base_question). The fault is what it tells a viewer about the product: the base reads as a different, black material, not the same pour as the ball.
findings.expected: A base that is plainly not glowing but still reads as dark Ember, about round 5's level: R 40-55, L* 5-6, C* about 25, with G and B under about 3 so the satin gets no grey sheen. The floor (left and front about L* 15) and the polished ball should stay as they are. The LIT-d light on the lamp and base only would do this if it lands there.

found.base_question:
The dark base reads right as a photograph of a lamp that is on in a dark studio. It does not read as smoke or frost. The body is a clean, very dark red with no grey veil: mean (22.2, 0.3, 0.2), G and B under 1. The cone still reads: the flanks fall to 0.82-0.86 of the centre (round 5: 0.82 and 0.78). The ball lights its top band (R up to 224). The base casts a dark contact shadow on a red-lit floor. The numbers also agree with each other: in linear light the flank is about 0.2 of the red on the floor beside it, as it should be for faces turned away from the ball.

But at 480 x 600 the body's colour is gone. It is L* 1.5, C* 7, and none of it reaches R 40 (round 5: 98 %). In the pair it sits within 1.5 L* of the pendant's black cap. Only the band under the ball says the base is red. Someone looking at the lit picture alone, and the owner, who looks closely at the base, will read it as a black or dark-brown base under a red ball. That misstates the 'same pour' base, which is why I rate it blocking with 'likely'.

My call: take the LIT-d alternative if, measured the same way, it meets all of these:
- The base body comes back to about round 5's level: R 40-55, L* 5-6, C* about 25.
- G and B stay under about 3. A grey satin sheen is what would read as smoke-frosted.
- The floor medians are unchanged, left and front about L* 15.
- The polished ball gets no new highlight.

If LIT-d cannot do all of that, r6's dark base is not wrong as a photograph: it is the true look of this lamp in the dark. The choice should then go to the owner with both frames side by side.
found.q1_pendant_ready: Yes. Pendant r6 reads as a real photograph of a lit pendant at 480 and at 100 %. The glow is clean, with no outlines in the high-pass (sigma-3 p99.9 4.95, round 5 9.8), even grain and Ember red (L* 39.1, C* 83.1, h 39.5). It matches the Core. Nothing clips. The cap is black and stepped, and the dark band under the cap holds. Only notes remain: cap and cord crushed to code 0, no halation, and a backdrop bright for a 'dark' room, matched in both frames.

The right floor still carries a neutral fill (L* 22.4 against 15.4 on the left), which is acceptable. If LIT-d lifts the base as described, without a grey sheen and without lighting the floor, take it. If not, the owner decides between that and r6's truthful dark base.

verdicts.measurement: I measured with my own code (verify-photo/v.py) on the same box, x 520-1110, y 1530-1740. Core r6 body at full size: mean sRGB (22.2, 0.29, 0.24), median L* 1.54, C* 7.05. At 480 (Lanczos): (22.2, 0.17, 0.10), L* 1.54, C* 7.06. At 480, 7 of 11,151 px reach R 40, all on the box's bottom two rows (lip and floor), so 'none' holds for the body. r5: (47.7, 1.00, 0.77), L* 5.88, C* 24.9; 98.9 % at R >= 40 (99.1 % at 480). OFF: (153.3, 34.7, 32.5), L* 34.2. Pendant cap at 480: L* 0.08 (lower step) to 0.84 (centre), C* about 0.1. So the base sits 0.7-1.5 L* above the cap, but about dE 7 from it, because the base has C* 7 and the cap none. NOT REPRODUCED: 'dark brown'. The hue is pure red (h_ab 19.6, G and B mean under 0.3, p99 2), and WebP q80 and JPEG q85 at 480 and 960 keep it at about (22, 0.4, 0.4), h 19.4. AGAINST 'a different material': at 480 the ball's own tint ring beside the opal measures (31-37, 5-7, 3-4), L* 3.6-4.5, C* 11-15, the same hue. PHYSICS: in linear red the body is 0.12-0.19 (flank strips) and 0.15-0.29 (centre) of the floor beside it. Crops: verify-photo/at480-x3-core5-core6-pendcap.png, ring-and-base-left-480-core6-core5-x3.png, page480-coreoff-core6.png, core6-base-full.png.
verdicts.reasoning: The observation is real. At 480 the base body is near-black and its colour is barely legible. What says it is red is the lit shoulder and a faint maroon cast, which shows beside the neutral pendant cap. Two parts of the finding do not hold. First, it is not brown: the hue is pure red, and still is after WebP or JPEG. Second, it does not read as a different material. The ball's own tint ring goes almost as dark (2-3 L* lighter, same hue), and in the 3x crop of the 480 frame the ball's shell and the base look like one dark pour with the opal glowing inside. The darkness is physically right, which the critic also says. The lamp page shows the OFF picture first, where the base is plainly red (153, 35, 33), so the page does not misstate the product. The critic's own fallback ('if LIT-d fails, r6 is not wrong; the owner chooses') is not a must-fix, so 'blocking' contradicts the critic's own call. I rate it a note: an owner's choice between r6 and LIT-d, shown side by side. LIT-d is better only if it passes the critic's four tests. I keep it rather than refute it because the owner looks closely at the base and may ask why it is black.

verified.base_check:
I agree with the critic's photographic verdict and with the fallback, but not with 'blocking'.

FULL SIZE (verify-photo/core6-base-full.png and foot-left-core6-core5-x3.png): the base is a clean, very dark oxblood.
- No grey veil: G and B mean 0.29 and 0.24, p99 2.
- No banding: R runs 14-35 with a smooth histogram. Denoiser mottling of +-1-2 R levels shows only under a 4x stretch (core6-base-Rstretch8-40.png).
- The foot edge is crisp, and the contact shadow on the red-lit floor is soft.
- The shoulder band reaches R 255 (p99 250 on the seat ring), not 'up to 224' as the critic says.
- The cone reads by its outline, its lit shoulder and its contact shadow. At y 1640 the left flank falls to 0.82 of the centre (sRGB), but the right only to 0.93 (r5: 0.86 and 0.77). So the right side is flatter than the critic's '0.82-0.86'.
- Linear flank-to-floor is 0.12-0.19, close to the critic's 'about 0.2' and right for faces turned away from the ball.

AT 480 (s480-core5-core6-pend6.png, page480-coreoff-core6.png, at480-x3-core5-core6-pendcap.png):
- 'Near-black with a faint maroon cast': yes. Body L* 1.5, C* 7.
- 'Dark brown': no. The hue is pure red, also after WebP q80 or JPEG q85.
- 'A black material different from the ball': no. The ball's own tint ring measures (31-37, 5-7, 3-4), L* 3.6-4.5, so the shell and the base go dark together and read as one pour (ring-and-base-left-480-core6-core5-x3.png).
- Beside the pendant's black cap the base is 0.7-1.5 L* lighter but about dE 7 away, because it is warm where the cap is neutral.
- On the page, the OFF picture comes first and shows the base plainly red.

So r6's dark base reads right for a lamp that is on in a dark studio and does not misstate the product. It is acceptable as it stands. Take LIT-d only if, measured the same way, it passes all four of the critic's tests:
- body R 40-55, L* 5-6, C* about 25;
- G and B under about 3;
- floor medians unchanged, left and front about L* 15;
- no new highlight on the polished ball.

Otherwise show the owner both frames side by side. Since he looks closely at the base, he should see both in any case.

found.base_question: The dark base reads right for a lamp that is on in a dark studio, and coming after the OFF picture it does not misstate the product. It is dark red, not grey or smoky: flank RGB about 21-23,0,0 with G and B at 0 and no sheen. The shoulder catches the ball's red light in a band that fades into the flank. The base also matches the dark maroon of the ball's own shell ring (31-37,2,1), so the lamp body reads as one pour gone dark. It is physically consistent too: base-to-floor luminance is 0.09 lit against 0.11 off, so it darkened with the room. Lifted 3 stops, it is a clean red satin cone with no smoke anywhere, so the owner's 'smoke-frosted' worry does not apply. But it does not show the base. At 480 x 600 it reads black (R 21 of 255; r5's 49,1,1 read dark red), the same tone as the pendant's black collar band (26,1,0). At full size it is a flat silhouette: L* 1.0-2.3 across the whole flank, with no satin, no shading and no foot band. A buyer who sees only this picture, or an owner who looks closely at the base, will see a black base rather than a red one in shadow.
found.q1_pendant_ready: Ready. At 480 x 600 and at 100 % the pendant reads as itself, switched on. It shows the black stepped cap on its black cord, the dark collar band under the cap, and the opal glowing through the tint with dome shading (L* 48.7 at the top to 25.5 at the bottom; 40.9 at the centre to 29-33 at the sides). Beyond the opal you see the darker shell edge, and at the rim the layered, polished lip, with a thin warm line where it reflects the floor. The r5 crackle is gone (glow detail std 1.58 against 2.26, and no outlines in a 12x stretch). No studio reflections remain, the glow matches the Core's, and the frame lines up with the OFF picture to 1 px. Only notes are left: the cap is crushed to 0 on 67 % of its pixels (the steps read by outline), and the band under the cap measures about 22 mm on the picture against the 13 mm stated.
found.q2_core_ready: LIT-c can be used as it stands, and nothing in it is false. The ball, opal, 10 mm rim ring (52 px at 5.14 px/mm) and polished seat lip all read right. The r5 crackle is gone (detail std 2.22 against 2.66, no outlines) and so is the bright left floor (15.4, was 38.8). The frame lines up with the OFF picture to 1 px. Its one cost is that the base reads black instead of red, at 480 x 600 and at full size. Given how closely the owner looks at the base, compare LIT-c and LIT-d side by side at 480 x 600. Use LIT-d only if its base reads dark red (around r5's L* 6, RGB about 49,1,1) and it passes three checks. (a) The floor at the foot gets the key's spill and a shadow of the base; a lit base on an unlit floor means light-linking, which looks pasted on and breaks the owner's first rule. verdicts.reasoning: I could not refute this finding. The place is right, every number reproduces, and it is not one of the known and accepted items. What I saw: at 480 x 600, alone and in the 1:1 strip, LIT-c's base is near-black. A faint maroon shows only against the brown floor or next to r5. The only clear red on the base is the lit band on the shoulder. r5's base at the same size plainly reads dark red. At 100 % the flank is a flat dark maroon silhouette. It fades from top to bottom under the shoulder band, but there is no satin, no left-right shading I can see (differences are about 0.3-0.5 L* at L* 1.5), and no foot band. Physics does not refute it, and the finding does not claim a physics error. Its fault is that the base is not shown. Two parts of the finding are overstated, and neither weakens the main point. (a) 'Lifted 3 stops ... with round shading': lifted, the cone is clean red with no grey, but its left-right shading is weak. The lower flank is flat (centre-to-edge 1.15 and 1.00, against r5's 1.21 and 1.42), so the cone reads by its outline and the shoulder band, not by shading. (b) 'The Hemisphere's black parts look alike': true for the collar band seen through the tint (R 7-58 gradient, median 30,1,0). It is not true for the cap and cord, which are 0,0,0 and look plainly blacker than the Core base side by side at 100 %. Severity: I would keep 'fix', not 'blocking'. At 480 it reads as a dark base on a lamp that is on in a dark room. It does not look CG, and on the page it comes right after the OFF picture, so it does not misstate the product there. The real fault shows when someone looks closely at the base, which the owner does: a flat silhouette where a red satin base should be.

verified.base_check: I agree with the critic on the substance: the base is physically consistent, dark red rather than grey or smoky, and it does not show the base. What I saw at 480 x 600 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b60/verify-product/v480-cl6.png and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b60/verify-product/v480-crops-co-cl5-cl6-pl6cap.png): a near-black cone with a strong red-lit band under the ball. Its outline stands out clearly against the floor, which is lit by the lamp (L* about 15, RGB about 55-58,31-34,27-29). The maroon in the flank is just visible against that floor and is obvious only next to r5, whose base reads dark red. What I saw at 100 % (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b60/verify-product/base100-cl6.png): a flat dark maroon (median 21,0,0, L* 1.5), G and B at 0, no sheen, no grey veil and no smoke. The red band at the shoulder fades into the flank over roughly 40-60 px. Below that the flank has no shading I can see and no foot band. Where the critic's answer holds: flank 21-23,0,0, G and B at 0; shell ring 31-37,2,1 (the base is about 1.7 L* darker than the ring); r5 49,1,1 and OFF 161,47,47 also match; luminance ratio 0.085 and 0.088 lit (left and front floor) against 0.10-0.13 off. Lifted 3 stops the cone is clean red. Three corrections. (1) The base did not simply darken 'with the room'. In the red channel its ratio to the floor fell from 0.36-0.45 (OFF) to 0.14-0.18 (LIT-c), and against the brighter right floor the luminance ratio is 0.051. That is still plausible geometry: the flank is near-vertical and sees the ball's overhang only at a grazing angle, while the floor faces the ball. But the 0.09 against 0.11 figure does not prove it on its own. (2) The lane's 'flank-to-centre ratios as good as before' does not reproduce. Centre-to-edge luminance is 1.33/1.21 on the upper flank and 1.15/1.00 on the lower flank, against r5's 1.42/1.69 and 1.21/1.42, so the shape reads by its outline and the shoulder band, not by shading. (3) The pendant's cap and cord are 0,0,0, plainly blacker than the Core base side by side (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b60/verify-product/core-base-vs-pend-cap-100.png). Only the collar band seen through the tint matches its tone. My answer to the open question: the dark base reads right as a lamp that is on in a dark studio, and after the OFF picture it does not misstate the product. Seen on its own, though, it reads as a black base under a red ball. It also offers nothing to an owner who studies the base, and it gives up the deep colour of the base. It is not smoke-frosted. If LIT-d meets the critic's 'expected' conditions (spill and a key shadow on the floor at the foot, no neutral sheen on the satin, no softbox in the ball or the polished lip), it is the better second picture. If it does not, LIT-c is the honest look and the OFF picture has to carry the base colour.
